Integrating the Beige Book with the March 15, 2020 FOMC statement: The policy action—cutting rates to 0–0.25%, launching sizable Treasury and MBS purchases, and expanding repo operations—aims to support credit and stabilize markets. However, Beige Book reports already show coronavirus-related weakness across Districts, including sharp hits to travel/tourism, transportation, and manufacturing via supply-chain disruptions, as well as stress in energy/natural resources. Activity in consumer and some nonresidential real estate segments varied but skewed softer, and loan growth showed signs of slowing. Incorporating SLOOS, banks tightened C&I/CRE standards (higher credit-score thresholds, reduced limits), demand weakened notably in construction and land development, and lenders anticipated further tightening amid deteriorating collateral values and HELOC performance. While some consumer credit (e.g., cards) looked steadier and Fed backstops mitigate market dysfunction, the Beige Book and SLOOS together point to procyclical credit headwinds that could blunt policy transmission and deepen near-term downside risks.
